meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bartender', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('white').

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'wine glass, champagne flute, goblet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We'll drink from our wine glasses.
She raised a glass of champagne.

examples.text: Ничего страшного! Мы из наших бокалов выпьем.
examples.trans: No problem! We'll drink from our wine glasses.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And what about the wine and fruit?

examples.text: Смотри, это электрогитара для Лёши. А тебе я взял чилийское вино и ягоды.
examples.trans: Look, this is an electric guitar for Lyosha. And for you I brought Chilean wine and berries.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

выпить.gloss: to drink (up); to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink of
meanings.note: + accusative or partitive genitive. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

Used without an object. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

examples.trans: May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: 'голову оторвать' = to tear someone's head off
meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cocktail' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какой коктейль ты будешь пить, Вика?
examples.trans: What cocktail will you drink, Vika?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, pretty, handsome').

examples.text: Красивая. Но это же не ваша жена! Я вашу жену видел.
examples.trans: She's pretty. But that's not your wife! I've seen your wife.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strong, sturdy, firm').

examples.text: Рука у тебя крепкая, как у деда.
examples.trans: Your grip is strong, just like your grandfather's.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

meanings.note: Сон is a dream while sleeping. Common feminine noun meaning 'dream, wish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, тебе сколько лет? Это глупые детские мечты.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, how old are you? Those are silly childish dreams.

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (on foot)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Серьёзно? = really?. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'juice' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will drink a little good juice.
Make me some fresh orange juice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным

+ infinitive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Short forms сух, суха, сухо, сухи. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ухой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dry').

examples.text: Нам нужны сухие дрова для костра.
examples.trans: We need dry firewood for the campfire.
The branch is dry! Look, our scout.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dance', paired with 'станцевать'.

examples.text: Ты у нас в клубе танцевала!

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.
